title: I Took a Night Job at a Lake Campground. There Was One Rule. #shorts #scarystories
description:
Count the tents at midnight. There are always twelve.

Follow for a new scary story every night.

#scarystory #horrorstories #creepy #shorts

beats.text: She knocked on my door all night, begging me to let her in. I'm glad I didn't.
Last summer, I took a night job at Pine Lake Campground.
The owner, Mr. Hale, gave me a little cabin by the water.
And one rule, that he made me save on my phone.
The first few weeks were perfect.
Families everywhere. Campfires. Kids roasting marshmallows.
Every night at midnight, I walked the shore and counted.
Twelve tents. Always twelve.
Then came the last night of August.
Almost everyone had gone home. Only one family was left.
But when I counted, I got thirteen.
The new tent stood at the edge of the water. No car. No fire. No footprints.
My phone buzzed. It was Mr. Hale.
I told him thirteen.
His answer came instantly.

overlay.message: NO. Lock your door. Don't open it for anyone until sunrise.

beats.text: So I locked myself in the cabin, and turned off the lights.
At two in the morning, someone knocked. Three slow knocks.
Then a little girl's voice said, please let me in. I can't find my mom.
I looked out the window.
A small figure stood on the dock, soaking wet, staring right at me.
Her smile was far too wide.
She knocked until dawn. I didn't open the door. I didn't sleep.
At sunrise, the thirteenth tent was gone. So was the last family.
Three days later, their faces were all over the news.
I quit that morning, and drove away without looking back.
A week later, Mr. Hale sent me one last message.

overlay.message: Thank you for keeping the door shut. The guard before you opened it.

beats.text: Nobody ever found that guard.
But this summer, Pine Lake is hiring again. And they're looking for two.
